messages:
maria: Quick sync — saw cold-start staleness on shard-12 after the rolling restart this morning. A bunch of small tenants returned stale prefixes for ~30s, then recovered. Anyone else see it?
jonathan: saw alerts. 504s from the runtime and some rehydrates taking a long time. curious if it's a KV replay ordering thing or just cold read penalty.
kevin: I think it's a corner of our rehydrate path + eviction policy. When a node restarts we evict most in-memory prefix slabs and rehydrate on demand; hot tenants try to rehydrate concurrently and saturate IO.
anya: was wondering if we should add a short soft-lock per-prefix during resync: cheap read-through that avoids parallel background rehydrates racing. e.g., first reader kicks off async fill and others block on a small in-memory future.
rahul: that helps reduce dup work but we're still vulnerable to the stale-response window if we serve from disk fallback before rehydrate completes. We need to decide correctness: do we allow slightly stale prefix reads during resync or block until fresh?
zach: SLA-wise, latency > errors. Prefer returning slightly stale data rather than error. But stale can break model inference if embeddings mismatch. tradeoff. :thinking_face: 
sre-bot: NOTE: rolling-restart on shard-12 completed at 5612339988. Degraded error rate peaked at +140% for 18m.
maria: Good point @zach. For some workloads stale prefix keys cause wrong predictions. We need per-tenant policy: best-effort stale vs strict-consistent. Could be a tenant config flag.
jonathan: alternative: maintain small on-disk snapshot TTL with version tag (epoch). If node restarts we serve from snapshot only if snapshot_epoch == cluster_epoch. If mismatch, 503-ish until resync or we fall back to a different replica.
kevin: implementable. We'd add an epoch header on prefix slabs. On read path: if slab.epoch < current_epoch => either (a) async repair + serve stale with warn-metric, or (b) reject.
anya: we already have a lease epoch for handoffs; piggybacking might be low-effort. But need to think about multi-replica divergence during rolling upgrades.
rahul: also watch eviction interplay: our eviction grace window can allow a recently-evicted prefix to be pulled from another node's cache. How do we avoid serving an old version? Maybe add per-prefix monotonic version (int) stored alongside data.
zach: versioning + epoch might be overkill for small prefixes. Can we do checksum + last-updated timestamp and a heuristic: if timestamp < threshold then trigger read-repair?
jonathan: heuristics OK short-term. long-term we need deterministic contract: read should be either consistent with a fence epoch or explicitly best-effort. Ops + product need to pick defaults.
maria: proposal: 3-mode behavior per tenant: strict (block until repaired), best-effort-stale (serve stale + emit metrics), fallback-replica (redirect to other healthy replica). Default => best-effort-stale.
kevin: implement plan: 1) add epoch tag to slabs, 2) add a prefix-level in-memory future to dedupe rehydrates, 3) emit metrics (stale_serves, repair_latency), 4) add tenant flag.
anyA: minor nit: make sure in-memory future has timeout and a fallback path, otherwise we risk head-of-line blocking.
rahul: Agree. Also add a background resync worker that opportunistically warms prefixes after restart but with heap/IO budget throttle.
sre-bot: FYI: added emf metric request: runtime.prefix_resync.duration and runtime.stale_serves.count.
deploy-bot: rolling canary: I'll push a canary build with epoch tags to shard-13 at 5612340600.
maria: ACTIONS: @kevin to prototype epoch-tag + dedupe future, @rahul to add background resync worker and throttles, @jonathan to draft tenant policy options and default. Can we target an experiment on shard-13 canary by EOD Friday?
zach: happy to help run canary and validate inference tests.
kevin: ack, starting spike today. will post short follow-up with perf numbers.``
